keyPoints: Question assumptions before accepting claims — apply this to the unit's own readings.
Distinguish fact, opinion and belief in any passage; examiners test this directly.
Modern family forms (nuclear, extended, single-parent) — know the terms.
Discuss change vs continuity: roles shift, emotional bonds remain.
Sports vocabulary (tournament, referee, endurance) appears in gap-fills — revise it.
Argument answers: sports build discipline and unity; give one counterpoint too.
Balance is the theme: benefits (communication, access) vs harms (addiction, privacy).
Use examples of digital etiquette when answering communication questions.
Education beyond schooling — critical mind and character, not just certificates.
Compare traditional and modern pedagogy with one example each.
Money vocabulary (inflation, budget, transaction) — often tested in word formation.
Ethics of money: wealth vs well-being; support with one textual argument.
Identify humour types: situational, verbal, irony — name the type then explain.
Humour often carries social criticism; state what is being mocked.
Culture is learned, shared and changing — three adjectives examiners expect.
Compare cultural practices across communities without judging them.
Link human activity to environmental consequence in every answer.
Know terms: ecosystem, sustainability, conservation — use them precisely.
CV and job-application language is tested — revise formal register and format.
Match personal skills to job requirements explicitly in answers.
Hobbies develop skills and identity — argue their value beyond entertainment.
Use hobby vocabulary (collecting, crafting, trekking) naturally in sentences.
Animal rights vs human use — present both positions before your own.
Note personification of animals in texts and what it reveals about humans.
History answers need evidence and perspective — whose story is told?
Connect historical events to present-day lessons for higher marks.
Rights are universal, inalienable and indivisible — memorise these three traits.
Give one local and one global example when discussing rights violations.
Distinguish leisure (free choice) from entertainment (consumption) in definitions.
Discuss screen time and well-being with balanced arguments.
Fantasy worlds follow internal logic — analyse the rules, not just the magic.
Symbolic reading: fantastic elements stand for real desires or fears.
Focus on human cost and moral choices, not battle details.
Peace-building answers: dialogue, justice, education — name concrete steps.
Music crosses language barriers — use this idea in discussion answers.
Describe music with precise vocabulary (rhythm, melody, harmony).
Push and pull factors frame every migration answer — use these terms.
Diaspora identity: belonging to two worlds; discuss the tension.
Power analysis: who holds it, how it is used, whom it affects — this three-step frame.
Political language (ideology, governance, authority) — define before using.
